papers.title: Design principles for entrepreneurial validation: An integrative review from a design science perspective
papers.abstract: Entrepreneurial validation is a central activity in entrepreneurship through which entrepreneurs collect and analyse information to validate assumptions about a potential market's needs, the appropriateness of the proposed solution, and/or the viability of the business model. Although research on entrepreneurial validation is growing, many studies approach it in isolation—as a singular test rather than an iterative design process. This paper presents an integrative review that synthesises design science research (DSR) principles with validation practices in entrepreneurship. We identify seven design principles that govern effective validation: (1) problem–solution fit primacy, (2) assumption explicitness, (3) iterative refinement, (4) stakeholder embeddedness, (5) evidence calibration, (6) scalability consideration, and (7) reflexive learning. These principles offer both a descriptive account of how validation works in practice and a prescriptive guide for practitioners and educators. By connecting DSR to entrepreneurial validation, we contribute a theoretically grounded framework that can support more systematic, design-driven entrepreneurship.
papers.summary_ja: デザインサイエンス研究と起業家的バリデーションを統合し、仮説検証を設計プロセスとして捉える7つのデザイン原則（問題・解決策フィット優先、仮定の明示化、反復的改善など）を提示した統合レビュー。

papers.title: Connected Friction—Collectively Designing Service Ecosystems Through Reflexive Relations
papers.abstract: Designing service ecosystems is a collective endeavor in which interdependent actors intentionally reconfigure the social structures coordinating their value cocreation. Because actors experience structures differently, however, they often disagree about how to reconfigure them. Although reflexivity—critical examination and transformative action on one's own thinking—is a key mechanism for designing service ecosystems, service research has focused mainly on reflexivity within single organizations, leaving multi-actor, ecosystem-level design underexplored. Drawing on reflexivity theory and practice-based design research, this paper develops a theoretical model of Connected Friction: a form of collective reflexivity in which actors purposely (re)configure their interpretations of social structures through collaborative encounters with disagreement. The model explains how actors can use friction—the discomfort that arises from encountering differing perspectives—as a catalyst for ecosystem-level learning and innovation. We illustrate the model through two cases: a healthcare service ecosystem in Norway and a smart city initiative in Sweden. The paper extends reflexivity theory to multi-actor service ecosystem contexts and provides design principles for practitioners engaged in collective ecosystem design.
papers.summary_ja: サービス・エコシステムの集団的デザインにおいて「Connected Friction（接続された摩擦）」という集合的リフレクション概念を提唱し、相互依存するアクターが意見の相違を触媒としてエコシステムレベルの学習・変革を促進するメカニズムを解明。

papers.title: Design probes as participatory tools for child-centred disaster risk reduction: An empirical study in Aotearoa New Zealand
papers.abstract: Disaster risk reduction (DRR) seeks to reduce the impacts of natural and socio-technical hazards on people and ecosystems. Although contemporary frameworks emphasise inclusive, whole-of-society participation, DRR education remains dominated by didactic instruction and top-down planning. Children, while directly affected by disasters, are rarely engaged as active agents in DRR planning and education. This paper presents an empirical study of design probes as participatory tools to engage children in DRR education in Aotearoa New Zealand. Design probes—open-ended, provocative artefacts designed to prompt users to reflect on their experiences, values and imaginaries—are adapted here to elicit children's perspectives on disaster risks and resilience-building. Data were gathered through probe activity kits deployed across three primary schools, supplemented by workshops and observations. The findings reveal how probe-based participation supports children's agency, local knowledge integration, and imaginative engagement with futures-oriented risk planning. The study contributes to participatory design methodology by demonstrating the potential of design probes to support inclusive, child-centred approaches in sociotechnical planning contexts.
papers.summary_ja: ニュージーランドの3小学校での実証研究を通じて、デザインプローブ（探索的参加型アーティファクト）が防災教育において子どもの主体的関与と地域知識統合、未来志向の思考を促進することを示した実証研究。

papers.title: Circular Business Model Innovation: A Systematic Review of Technology and Resource Strategy Choices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite growing scholarly interest in circular business model innovation (CBMI), established frameworks are applied inconsistently: Few empirical studies specify how they conceptualise CBMs or the scope and degree of novelty of the business model changes reported, raising construct validity concerns. This systematic review synthesises 94 empirical studies and proposes a consolidated typology of circular business models (CBMs) organised along two dimensions: technology strategy (product life extension vs. material cycling) and resource strategy (product service systems vs. value chain integration). We map how firms transition between CBM types and identify organisational capabilities that enable these transitions. The review reveals that radical CBMI is rare: Most studies report incremental changes within existing CBM archetypes. We also find significant gaps in research on B2B contexts and cross-sector CBM adoption, suggesting important avenues for future research. Our typology provides a common vocabulary for researchers and practitioners seeking to systematically compare, evaluate and design circular business models.
papers.summary_ja: 94件の実証研究のシステマティックレビューを通じて、循環型ビジネスモデルイノベーション（CBMI）を2×2タイポロジーで整理し、急進的CBMIが稀なことと移行を促す組織能力を特定。

papers.title: The Futures Thinking Kite scenario method
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop the Futures Thinking Kite as a scenario method using a visual heuristic to examine four conditional relationships between intervention intensity and desirable outcomes. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper draws on futures studies, systems thinking and scenario planning traditions to develop and illustrate the Futures Thinking Kite method. The method is illustrated through two application examples: climate policy and digital health governance. Findings The Kite method produces four distinct scenarios labelled Drift, Transform, Optimize, and Sustain—each corresponding to different combinations of intervention strength and system responsiveness. The method's visual and intuitive design lowers the barrier for non-expert participants to engage in futures thinking. The paper also proposes a facilitation guide for workshops. Research limitations/implications The paper presents a conceptual proposal rather than a longitudinal empirical validation. Future research should test the method in real organisational settings. Practical implications The Kite method provides practitioners with a simple, visual scenario tool adaptable to different policy and business contexts, complementing existing scenario methods such as the 2x2 matrix and causal layered analysis.
papers.summary_ja: 介入強度と望ましい成果の4つの条件的関係（Drift/Transform/Optimize/Sustain）を視覚的に検討する「Futures Thinking Kite」シナリオ手法を提案。非専門家でも活用できるワークショップファシリテーションガイドを提示。

papers.title: Exploration Across Incompatible Technologies: How Firms Organize Flexibility for Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Firms often face multiple emerging technologies that evolve in parallel yet share limited architectural compatibility. In such settings, firms may concentrate innovation on one trajectory or pursue flexibility by maintaining engagement across multiple trajectories. We theorize that flexibility can improve innovation performance, but that these benefits depend on organizational structures that facilitate deep, trajectory-specific learning and effective coordination. We argue that focused organizational units enable concentrated learning within each technology trajectory, while cross-functional integration mechanisms bridge insights across trajectories. Using longitudinal panel data from 143 semiconductor firms over 23 years, we demonstrate that firms achieving high levels of both focused units and integration mechanisms outperform those relying on either alone. Our findings advance understanding of how firms can build innovation flexibility without sacrificing the depth of expertise required to compete in nascent technology domains.
papers.summary_ja: 半導体企業143社・23年間のパネルデータを用い、アーキテクチャ的に非互換な複数の新興技術を並行探索する際は「集中型組織ユニット＋クロスファンクショナル統合」の組み合わせが最高の革新成果をもたらすことを実証。

papers.title: The cost of the buzz? A sufficiency threshold perspective on digital transformation disclosure and cost of equity capital
papers.abstract: Firms disclose information about complex internal activities to keep capital markets informed about their long-term value. We engage two rival predictions, the 'more-is-better' assumption in information risk theory and the 'more-is-noisy' assumption in technological fad perspectives, and ask what should be the optimal scope of digital transformation disclosure. We examine 613 firms' annual reports over five years using a novel text-based measure of digital transformation disclosure. Using threshold regression methods, we find that the relationship between digital transformation disclosure and cost of equity capital follows a non-linear, inverted-U pattern, peaking at a sufficiency threshold beyond which additional disclosure increases rather than reduces capital costs. Our findings suggest that firms face a 'buzz premium'—a market penalty for excess hype in transformation narratives—and that over-disclosure signals managerial overconfidence or a lack of strategic clarity. These findings have practical implications for investor relations, strategic communication and digital transformation management.
papers.summary_ja: 613社の年次報告書分析から、DX開示量と資本コストが逆U字型の関係にあり、十分性閾値を超えると「バズプレミアム」（過剰ハイプへの市場ペナルティ）が発生することを実証。

papers.title: The Rose and Its Hidden Thorn: Patterning and Evolution of Consumer Vulnerability in Transformative Service Initiatives
papers.abstract: Transformative Service Initiatives (TSIs) aim to reduce consumer vulnerability (CV), yet they can reproduce the harm they seek to address. We investigate this paradox in TSIs offering entrepreneurship support to refugees. Study 1, drawing on interviews with forty-two managers from thirty-three TSIs, uncovers three patterns of consumer vulnerability: Latent Fragility (structural risk factors that TSIs overlook), Induced Brittleness (vulnerability created by the TSI itself), and Persistent Marginality (entrenched inequalities that TSIs fail to overcome). Study 2 offers a process model of CV evolution, tracing how TSIs interact with these patterns over time. The combined findings reveal systemic blind spots in TSI design and call for a more reflexive, vulnerability-aware approach to transformative service design. The paper contributes to transformative service research by developing a typology of CV patterns and a process model of CV evolution.
papers.summary_ja: 難民支援TSI（Transformative Service Initiative）33組織への42名インタビューから、サービスが意図せず消費者脆弱性を再生産する3パターン（潜在的脆弱性・誘発的脆弱性・持続的疎外）とその時間的進化プロセスモデルを構築。

papers.title: Mediating value tensions in transitions: A valuation perspective on innovation systems
papers.abstract: Transition studies, and technological innovation systems (TIS) more specifically, have remained rather implicit about how innovation trajectories are shaped by value concerns. Attention in literature has mostly been limited to innovating actors' unambiguous goals of decarbonisation. In order to explicitly address a multitude of conflicting value concerns expressed in diverse contexts, we propose conceptual extensions to the TIS approach. Building on recent innovation systems and sociology literature, we conceptualise innovation systems as 'valuation arrangements' – sets of devices, actors and practices that make different values visible, commensurable and actionable in the context of an innovation system. We illustrate our framework with the case of green hydrogen innovation in Europe and show how valuation arrangements can serve as a mediating mechanism for navigating value pluralism in transitions.
papers.summary_ja: 技術イノベーションシステム（TIS）論を「バリュエーション・アレンジメント」として拡張し、グリーン水素イノベーションを事例に相反する価値観が共存する移行プロセスにおける調停メカニズムを解明。
